item.title: Greek state, federation president back immediate transition and elections
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
Elections loom in Greece as the state and the new Hellenic Basketball Federation president seek a transitional cleanup

The post Greek state, federation president back immediate transition and elections appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

The deputy sports minister of Greece, Giannis Vroutsis, has recommended that the new administration of the Hellenic Basketball Federation proceed with elections as quickly as possible.

Following a meeting with EOK officials on Monday that lasted less than an hour, Vroutsis issued this strong recommendation. Due to the self-governing nature of the federation, the state cannot legally intervene to force elections, as such an action would trigger a severe reaction from FIBA.

“Today, I urgently called the new president and the board of directors of the basketball federation. I told them that the public’s trust has been shaken,” stated the 63-year-old politician. “I respect the autonomy of the federation, and I do not impose. I recommend holding elections as soon as possible, immediately if it is feasible.”

“Until the management audits are completed, financial aid to the federation, and only to the federation, is frozen,” added Vroutsis. Earlier in the day, he pledged that ‘light will be shed on EOK’s finances’, stressing that ‘we have a collective duty to restore the credibility of the league and the sport’.

In response, newly appointed president Angelos Papanikolaou confirmed the intention to transition toward an election. “We are aligned in our approach toward a cleanup,” he mentioned, explaining that the current board will serve in a transitional capacity to ensure the smooth continuation of domestic leagues and national team activities. “We are proposing to the ministry a charter for the holding of the Hellenic Basketball Federation elections.”

This intervention follows a major crisis in Greece, marked by the pre-trial detention of Vangelis Liolios amid the unfolding match-fixing and bribery scandal.

item.title: Ataman reacts to Greece scandal: “Following by shock all the news”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
Greece's match-fixing and bribery scandal captures the attention of 60-year-old Ergin Ataman

The post Ataman reacts to Greece scandal: “Following by shock all the news” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Former Panathinaikos Aktor head coach Ergin Ataman expressed his deep shock regarding the major corruption scandal currently shaking Greece.

Speaking during a visit to Athens, where the investigation has led to the pre-trial detention of prominent officials, including the former president of the Hellenic Basketball Federation, Vangelis Liolios, the Turkish tactician shared his perspective on the unfolding events and his enduring connection to the Greens.

“Hello. I am in Athens and following by shock all the news, but I’m sorry that it would not be appropriate for me to express an opinion on a matter that is currently before the judiciary,” he reflected regarding the ongoing proceedings during a text exchange with the Greek television network ANT1.

“Panathinaikos is a very big club and will take whatever steps are necessary regarding this issue,” continued Ataman, turning his attention to his former club, expressing full confidence in the organization’s leadership moving forward. “I like to send all Panathinaikos and real sports lovers my love and greetings.”

The Istanbul native also explicitly highlighted his appreciation for club owner Dimitris Giannakopoulos, “I love Dimitris and his passion for Panathinaikos and Greek sports,” he added.

Ataman’s deep ties to the Greek powerhouse stem from a successful multi-year tenure that concluded in June. Under his guidance, Panathinaikos returned to the absolute pinnacle of Europe, capturing the EuroLeague championship in 2024 alongside domestic League and Cup trophies.

Currently serving as the head coach of the Turkish senior national team, the 60-year-old expert remains heavily invested in the continental community.

item.title: Jalen Williams stretchered off court after devastating leg injury
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
The Oklahoma City Thunder depth is facing an early test in the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season, particularly after losing Jalen Williams

The post Jalen Williams stretchered off court after devastating leg injury appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Jalen Williams sustained a severe lower left leg injury late in the Oklahoma City Thunder’s victory over the LA Clippers on Sunday, turning a 3–0 start in the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season into a somber affair.

With just over a minute remaining, the 25-year-old guard-forward drove hard to the rim and collapsed as his limb buckled unnaturally under his weight. Medical staff rushed out, quickly covering the area with towels. After a tense delay, emergency personnel wheeled him off the court. Williams offered a double thumbs-up from the stretcher, prompting a standing ovation.

The arena initially went cold. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander pulled his jersey over his face and later fought back tears, promising the team would hold down the fort. Head coach Mark Daigneault looked visibly shaken at the podium. “Those are tough, man,” he mentioned. “We’re not doing great.”

The Thunder roster was already dealing with injuries, including Serbian Nikola Topic sidelined by back surgery, but now faces an immediate crisis. Before the catastrophic finish, Jaylin Williams exited with a sore right wrist, and Cason Wallace left with a shoulder issue.

Official updates remain scarce. While early accounts debated whether the knee or ankle took the brunt of the impact, replays pointed toward a severe lower-leg fracture or dislocation. Complete medical evaluations are expected Monday morning.

The team has no time to process. They host the Phoenix Suns on Monday evening to complete a back-to-back and begin a long stretch without one of their cornerstone players.

item.title: Rudy Gobert rejects style adjustments: “I am the best in the world”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
A revamped and trash-talking Minnesota Timberwolves squad does not budge experienced big Rudy Gobert

The post Rudy Gobert rejects style adjustments: “I am the best in the world” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Following a dominant win over the Toronto Raptors at Target Center on Sunday, Minnesota Timberwolves starter Rudy Gobert made it clear that his approach remains steady despite his team’s evolving style.

When asked if he has altered his game to fit the current roster, he rejected the idea.

“My role is the same,” he replied. “My role is to be who I am, be the best in the world at what I do. And then offensively just dominate, dominate, dominate in my own way, with my running, with my screening, my offensive rebound.”

The 14-year veteran big also addressed the vocal nature of a squad that has quickly gained a reputation for competitive banter.

“We don’t want to be a team that talks too much. I think talk is cheap, but we just got to talk enough,” he mentioned. “Ant and a few more guys, without naming them, they get going by talking a little bit, so I think that’s a good thing as long as we back it up.”

The undefeated Wolves look to sustain this momentum on Monday when they face the Cleveland Cavaliers at Rocket Arena. So far, 34-year-old Gobert has chipped in 9.0 points and 12.3 rebounds per contest.

A dominant force inside, the Saint-Quentin native is a three-time All-Star and four-time Defensive Player of the Year, as well as a veteran of 1,004 appearances in the league. This career is expanding within one of the top defenses, marking the pursuit of his first championship.

item.title: Fasoulas: “The reality now is the existence of a criminal organization”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
A statement by Panagiotis Fasoulas regarding recent developments in Greece

The post Fasoulas: “The reality now is the existence of a criminal organization” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Panagiotis Fasoulas has spoken out on the developments shaking the Hellenic Basketball Federation, shortly following the confirmed pre-trial detention of former president Vangelis Liolios on Sunday.

In a written statement shared on social media, the Greek basketball legend characterized the current era as the ‘darkest period’ and called for an immediate investigation into past federation elections.

“We are undisputedly in the darkest period for the sport of basketball, a sport that has always been synonymous with national achievements and national pride. Recent judicial rulings have proven that the whispers and insinuations of previous years regarding actions, individuals, and their role within EOK were entirely well-founded. The reality now is the existence of a criminal organization within the Hellenic Basketball Federation.

In the 2021 EOK elections, together with Fanis Christodoulou, Memos Ioannou, and other associates, all highly accomplished figures in the sport, we submitted an alternative proposal for the evolution and prospects of Greek basketball. In this endeavor, we had Nikos Galis and Panagiotis Giannakis by our side.

The results, however, did not justify our efforts. In the subsequent elections in 2024, and while the Liolios administration had already given ‘samples of its work’, Mr. Liolios and the board members of his faction recorded—paradoxically—an even higher percentage.


As if that were not enough, both during and after the elections, a coordinated effort was unleashed to personally ridicule, discredit, and annihilate my personality within the basketball world.

I believe that now that the abscess is bursting, the investigation must be extended to both electoral processes of 2021 and 2024, which were conducted via electronic voting rather than in person, following Mr. Liolios’s insistence. In these elections, he recorded percentages that cannot be explained by logic or by the actual dynamics of the electoral body.

During my tenure as a board member until 2024, even though from a certain point onward I abstained from the meetings of a body whose members only knew the word ‘yes’, I exposed in every possible way the lack of transparency, the political favoritism treated as normalcy, and the corruption of consciences, phenomena that served as the ‘banners’ of the Liolios administration from day one. I continued to do the same after the 2024 elections, where I was not even elected as a board member.

From grandiose proclamations ‘about children who will never cry again’, we have ended up with school basketball games being the subject of a prosecutorial investigation. Meritocracy surpassed all boundaries with the invention of the so-called ‘Wild Cards’, through which teams were relegated on the court yet ultimately remained in the division, while teams that earned promotion were bypassed by others that legally deserved to move up.

Furthermore, I remind everyone that all decisions were taken unanimously by a board of directors comprised of individuals who functioned, and seek to continue functioning, as ‘puppets’ of the now-former president.

Regarding current developments, I believe that Greek basketball and the people who truly love and serve it are devastated.

To immediately reverse the climate of distrust that has been created and to restore the prestige of the sport as much as possible, we, the people who come from the very core of the sport, as well as the state, must proceed with a radical breakthrough.

A breakthrough that will contribute to the purging of the current state of decay, while simultaneously moving forward to the next day.

A next day that must be built on transparency, legality, and equality before the law for each and every person in basketball.”

item.title: Hezonja goes viral by waving off Cavaliers play: “I’m here”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
The Cleveland Cavaliers are benefiting immensely from Mario Hezonja's veteran experience

The post Hezonja goes viral by waving off Cavaliers play: “I’m here” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Mario Hezonja is making plenty of noise, especially with demanding court awareness from his Cleveland Cavaliers teammates.

During a media session ahead of Saturday’s matchup against the Brooklyn Nets at Rocket Arena, the 31-year-old Croatian forward opened up about his return to the NBA after winning a EuroLeague title in 2023. Now playing under head coach Kenny Atkinson, he is averaging 9.5 points and 4.0 rebounds, helping his squad to an early 1–1 record.

Reviewing the previous loss to the Philadelphia 76ers at Xfinity Mobile Arena on Thursday, Hezonja focused heavily on taking care of the ball. In the NBA, leads evaporate quickly. This reality contrasts with his previous environment.

“In Europe you might struggle to come back from a large lead, but here the game is so fast,” explained the Dubrovnik native. “You got to treat it as a 10-point lead or not lead at all, mentally.”

Taking accountability

Hezonja praised Atkinson and the coaching staff for their approach to teaching the players. However, he refuses to use roster turnover as an excuse for poor execution. When opponents switch up their defensive looks, he expects the players to solve the puzzle themselves.

“It’s five of us on a court, and you need to read those situations,” he said. “Absolutely nobody cares that we have new people. It’s just everybody has to start to click as soon as possible because that’s going to give us extra wins.”

That mindset showed when Hezonja waved off a play call to run the offense himself. He did it to protect Donovan Mitchell. The two veterans have a long history. His teammate backed him instantly.

“You’re not supposed to bring up the ball against the pressure because we need you in the last quarter,” he shared his message to 30-year-old Mitchell. “We need you in the Playoffs, we need you in game 80, game 60.”

The experienced forward wants to absorb that contact instead. By handling the ball, screening, and playing defense, he intends to preserve Mitchell, James Harden, Evan Mobley, and Jarrett Allen for April. “As much pressure that I can take off of them is just going to be so beneficial,” he stressed.

No rookie nerves

The transition back to North America has been surprisingly simple. Hezonja credited everyone in the organization for embracing him as both a player and a person.

He still enjoys the classic theatrics in the NBA, pointing out the announcer shouting ‘Cavaliers’ through bursts of real fire during pregame introductions. But once the ball is tipped, the spectacle fades. When asked if he had a sentimental moment realizing he was finally back in the league, Hezonja shook his head. He does not feel like a rookie anymore.

“Not at all,” he confessed. “It was so weird. As a rookie, everything is new. You try to score and do all these things. But now? Nothing. Just a basketball game. Absolutely no feelings whatsoever.”

item.title: Matas Buzelis fights through flu-like symptoms: “No excuse”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
A high-energy demand pairing with health issues complicates the start of the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season for Matas Buzelis

The post Matas Buzelis fights through flu-like symptoms: “No excuse” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Chicago Bulls forward Matas Buzelis revealed he has been battling flu-like symptoms following a loss to the Washington Wizards at the United Center. Despite the setback, the 22-year-old Lithuanian scored 21 points on 7-of-13 shooting. However, a defeat dropped his side to 1–2 to start the 2026–27 Regular Season.

Buzelis admitted his conditioning was not optimal during the opening week, where he averaged 12.0 points over his first two outings. He also sat out the fourth quarter of the second game.

“To be honest, I haven’t been feeling like myself,” he mentioned, noting he was dealing with a little sickness. “This is no excuse.”

Buzelis felt a breakthrough during Saturday’s contest.

“I felt like today it’s gone away. I felt like way more like myself, and I’m still trying to adjust to how our team plays. I know I can figure it out. It’s just all part of the process. All the coaches believe in me to do that, and I put the work in, and it’ll happen, I know,” he explained.

Beyond his health, the Chicago native is adjusting to a demanding role under new head coach Tiago Splitter. Looking to crash the glass aggressively, Buzelis acknowledged this responsibility takes a lot of energy.

“You have to jump, and then you have to run back because the guys are running. When teams realize that another team is crashing, they’re going to get out in transition, and you’ve got to run back. To be honest, the hardest part is being in shape and keeping consistently going,” he said.

The Bulls resume action against the Boston Celtics at TD Garden on Monday.

item.title: Queta brings Portuguese shooting flair to Boston: “Good to see one”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
Hoping for more from beyond the arc, 27-year-old Neemias Queta enjoys celebrating a make of his own for once

The post Queta brings Portuguese shooting flair to Boston: “Good to see one” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Boston Celtics center Neemias Queta is working to expand his offensive range, reflecting on his progress after Sunday’s practice ahead of a back-to-back stretch in the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season.

The corner triple against the New York Knicks on Friday was his first conversion of the young season. It marked a distinct step forward for the 7-foot big, who finished the entire previous campaign shooting just 1-of-8 from deep.

“Really good,” the 27-year-old center responded when asked how it felt to connect. “Used to being on the bench and guys celebrating in front of you, so getting to do that in front of them too for once is pretty nice, and hopefully I get more.”

The former champion and first Portuguese player in league history previously discussed stretching the floor during training camp, but he remains grounded.

“It’s just one. It’s a game of makes and misses,” Queta said. “Can’t really get too happy about one, like I wouldn’t be too down about a bunch of misses too. Good to see one going in, but tomorrow there’s another game. That’s, that’s what I’m focused on.”

Perimeter shooting isn’t entirely new to him, tracing back to his early playing days.

“Back in the day, back in Portugal, I used to do that too,” he explained. “It’s something I’m comfortable doing. It’s not that new for me, but I think it’s just getting unrusty at it. Figure out the right moments to shoot, figuring out whether it’s better options coming up, whether some more action that we can get into on the backside and stuff like that.”

The C’s sit at 1–1, tied for eighth in the Eastern Conference. They host the Chicago Bulls on Monday and the Brooklyn Nets on Tuesday at TD Garden.

Queta leads a European group on the roster that includes Luka Garza, Hugo Gonzalez, and Amari Williams.

item.title: NBA Roundup: Wagner stars at MSG, Thunder lose three players
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
Several unfortunate injuries mark a seven-game slate in the NBA

The post NBA Roundup: Wagner stars at MSG, Thunder lose three players appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

The Oklahoma City Thunder moved to 3-0 on the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season by beating the Los Angeles Clippers 108–101 at Paycom Center. But victory felt incredibly heavy. They lost three players to injuries, including Jalen Williams leaving the floor on a stretcher and his left leg draped in towels. Before that, Jaylin Williams exited with a sore right wrist, and Cason Wallace walked off with a sore left shoulder, with Serbian Nikola Topic already out following low back surgery.

Shai Gilgeous-Alexander carried the offense with 34 points. Belgian Ajay Mitchell provided a massive lift off the bench, bringing energy to log 18 points, six rebounds, four assists, and three steals. German starter Isaiah Hartenstein posted a 12-point, 12-rebound double-double, with Spanish backup Aday Mara at two points and three rebounds in his 14 minutes. For the Clips, European action was limited to Spanish Baba Miller, who grabbed one rebound during a two-minute stint.

At Madison Square Garden, the Orlando Magic handled business with a 111–102 win, pushing the defending champions New York Knicks to an unexpected 0–3 start. German starter Franz Wagner completely ran the floor in the final quarter, dropping 21 of his 23 points. He finished just one assist shy of a triple-double, adding 13 rebounds and nine assists to his stat line. “I was pretty aggressive,” the 25-year-old forward explained during his postgame press conference, when asked about tweaks to trigger the late explosion. “I was just making bad reads out there the first three quarters.”

Fellow German Tristan da Silva poured in 19 points, including five shots from deep. Montenegrin Nikola Vucevic added five points, three rebounds, and two blocks in limited minutes, but Georgian Goga Bitadze did not play.

Anthony Black scored 18 points in his return after missing the first two games with an ankle injury. His strong performance provided a much-needed boost, especially since star forward Paolo Banchero recently joined French prospect Noah Penda on the injury list. Health concerns deepened late in Sunday’s game when Jalen Suggs landed awkwardly on a fast-break layup. He collapsed and immediately grabbed his right leg in pain before ultimately exiting to a warm ovation from the MSG crowd.

For the Knicks, British starter OG Anunoby fought hard for 22 points, pouring in ten in the final period. His French teammates, Mohamed Diawara and Pacome Dadiet, did not get into the game.

Rajakovic loss, Iisalo win

Meanwhile, the Toronto Raptors had to play without Kawhi Leonard due to knee swelling. Led by Serbian head coach Darko Rajakovic, they fell 117–94 to the Minnesota Timberwolves. “You’ve always got to be ready for those situations and adjust,” noted 47-year-old Rajakovic about missing his star. “He’s a big part of what we do, but it’s a great opportunity for everybody else to step up.”

His Austrian starter Jakob Poeltl grabbed only one rebound. Opposite 31-year-old Poeltl, the French duo impacted the game for the Wolves. Starter Rudy Gobert logged eight points and 13 rebounds, while reserve Joan Beringer chipped in six points and six boards in 13 minutes.

Finnish play-caller Tuomas Iisalo guided the Memphis Grizzlies to a 123–112 win over the Sacramento Kings at Golden 1 Center. Ty Jerome once more paved the way with 31 points, while Dutch Quinten Post tallied seven points and five rebounds. For Sacramento, Lithuanian star Domantas Sabonis put up 15 points and 15 rebounds for the hosts, with Israeli reserve Emanuel Sharp finishing with three points.

Finally, the Detroit Pistons took down the Philadelphia 76ers 106–93 despite losing Isaiah Joe early to a hip injury and previously ruling out Jalen Duren for at least two weeks due to a hamstring strain. Turkish Adem Bona provided a bright spot for Philly off the bench, picking up six points, 13 rebounds, and three blocks, but French teammate Rayan Rupert did not play.

item.title: Ivica Zubac sprains ankle in Pacers blowout win over Nets
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
The Indiana Pacers extend the winless start of Spanish head coach Jordi Fernandez, but lose Ivica Zubac

The post Ivica Zubac sprains ankle in Pacers blowout win over Nets appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

The Indiana Pacers dominated on Sunday night, hammering the Brooklyn Nets 136–109 at Barclays Center. Tyrese Haliburton led the charge with 24 points and ten assists.

However, the win came with a price. Croatian Ivica Zubac played just seven minutes. With 4:57 left in the opening period, the 29-year-old big stepped on Kelly Oubre Jr.’s foot while chasing a rebound, spraining his left ankle. Zubac left the floor with two points, two assists, and one rebound. He later exited the arena on crutches.

Postgame, head coach Rick Carlisle shared an update on his starting center. With the x-ray negative but the ankle swollen, the 66-year-old tactician said it is unlikely Zubac will play Monday against the Milwaukee Bucks.

Defensive woes

The loss drops Brooklyn to 0–3 to start the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season. Coached by Spanish Jordi Fernandez, the group struggled to contain Indiana’s perimeter shooters. Despite the blowout, a few European prospects provided bright spots.

French guard Nolan Traore tallied 17 points, five assists, and two blocks. German Moritz Wagner provided additional punch off the bench, registering 13 points in 14 minutes. Russian starter Egor Demin added three points and two steals, while Israeli Danny Wolf tallied six points, and fellow Israeli Ben Saraf chipped in two points in brief action.

“This one really got away after the first quarter. We had the right intentions. We’re on the first back-to-back of the season, and there’s no excuses here,” Fernandez admitted, reflecting on the defensive collapse. “I’m not going to blame my players. I’m going to blame myself.”

“Just wanted to help the team with my strength, touching the paint, making plays,” mentioned 20-year-old Traore. “That’s the main thing. My teammates set good screens on me, and I’m able to make reads.”

item.title: Doncic powers Lakers with 52 points: “Just get out and run”
item.dc:creator: Giannis Askounis
item.description:
A dominating 52-point showing for Luka Doncic sends the Los Angeles Lakers to 3–0 in the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season

The post Doncic powers Lakers with 52 points: “Just get out and run” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Johnny Askounis/ info@eurohoops.net

Luka Doncic delivered a spectacular 52-point performance on Sunday powering the Los Angeles Lakers to a hard-fought 132–123 victory over the Utah Jazz at the Delta Center.

The Slovenian superstar shot 17-of-30 from the field, including eight three-pointers. He added ten assists, eight rebounds, and two steals in 38 minutes of action. This victory pushed his side to a perfect 3–0 start for the 2026–27 NBA Regular Season. It also marked their eighth win in their last nine meetings opposite Utah.

The Lakers had to fight back after trailing by as many as 18 points in the second quarter. They finally grabbed their first lead just before halftime. Doncic buried a signature stepback three-pointer with 4.1 seconds remaining in the period to get them there. When the game tightened late in the fourth quarter, Luka Magic took over once again. He capped off a decisive 14–5 run by hitting back-to-back shots from beyond the arc.

“Just be solid, be physical on the defensive end,” he mentioned in a postgame interview, describing how the team coached by JJ Redick overcame their slow start. “Then just get out and run. Play the best we know how to play. We are learning our lesson, so we cannot start games like this anymore.”

Historic milestones

Doncic became the first Laker to record at least 50 points and ten assists in a single game since Elgin Baylor accomplished the feat in 1963. He is only the third player in franchise history to do so.

The game also marked the tenth 50-point performance of his career. Since he entered the NBA in 2018, only James Harden and Damian Lillard have recorded more.

Furthermore, this was his 19th 40-point game with the storied franchise. The Ljubljana native passed LeBron James for sole possession of sixth place.

Markkanen drops 28

Complementing Doncic, Austin Reaves stepped up with a crucial 29-point contribution. Off the bench, Georgian Sandro Mamukelashvili provided valuable frontcourt minutes, chipping in nine points, three rebounds, and a block. Center Walker Kessler made his return to Utah after being sent to Los Angeles in a July sign-and-trade deal, finishing the night with two points and seven rebounds.

On the wrong end of the scoreboard, Finnish Lauri Markkanen led the way with a team-high 28 points on 9-of-20 shooting. He hit five three-pointers and grabbed seven rebounds in a 37-minute shift. Ukrainian reserve Sviatoslav Mykhailiuk also appeared off the bench, adding two points and three rebounds in 13 minutes.

Looking ahead, the Jazz will quickly get a chance to bounce back as they host the Memphis Grizzlies on Monday, while the Lakers return home to face the Portland Trail Blazers on Tuesday.

item.title: EuroLeague president Dejan Bodiroga’s party wins the Serbian parliamentary elections
item.dc:creator: Stefan Acevski
item.description:
The first results of the parliamentary elections in Serbia are known, and the party of which Dejan Bodiroga is a member has won the elections

The post EuroLeague president Dejan Bodiroga’s party wins the Serbian parliamentary elections appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Stefan Acevski / info@eurohoops.net

A significant change occurred in the Serbian elections as the ruling party SNS lost power, and it was taken over by the Students list.

Among the candidates of the Students’ List is Dejan Bodiroga, the president of the EuroLeague, and according to initial estimates, his list won 52% of the votes, or about 135 seats in the Serbian parliament.

“Today, above all, Serbia is fighting for freedom and for the return of a country that has been hijacked,” Bodiroga told reporters in Belgrade earlier in the day.

The ruling party won about 39%, or around 104 seats, in the Serbian parliament, which has 250 members.

Bodiroga was very active during the campaign, frequently staying in Serbia and appearing at the largest gatherings of the anti-regime party, and in recent weeks, he was one of the main speakers at most of these events.

By the end of the year, Serbia is also facing presidential elections, as Aleksandar Vucic’s second term expired in September this year. The elections are expected to take place in December, and Dejan Bodiroga is mentioned as one of the potential candidates from the list that won the parliamentary elections.

item.title: Greek sports minister to meet with Greek federation board and new president Aggelos Papanikolaou
item.dc:creator: Aris Barkas
item.description:
Greek sports minister Giannis Vroutsis will meet in a few hours the new board of the Greek federation to set a roadmap for the future

The post Greek sports minister to meet with Greek federation board and new president Aggelos Papanikolaou appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Aris Barkas/ barkas@eurohoops.net

The investigation into the Greek basketball scandal is still pending; however, the board elected a new president since Vaggelis Liolios is out of the picture, and tomorrow they will meet with Greek sports minister Giannis Vroutsis.

Aggelos Papanikolaou was elected as the new president from the 23-member board in an extraordinary meeting.

Papanikolaou was an opponent of Liolios in the 2021 elections for the presidency; in the recent 2025 elections, he was on Liolios’ side, running for a spot on the federation board.

The intention of the sports ministry, however, seems to be for the whole board to resign and for a personality with wide acceptance in the basketball world, like Panagiotis Giannakis, to take over.

Former player Periklis Dorkofikis, who played for Olympiacos and AEK in the past, was added to the board today as a runner-up from the previous elections, filling up the empty spot left by Liolios stepping down and he already made a public statement on his social media asking for the board to resign and get a fresh start.

Meanwhile, the federation board announced six points of commitment for the future, including the uninterrupted continuation of the season in all national leagues, support to the national teams, especially for the upcoming FIBA Windows, initiatives for the improvement of referees, integrity safeguards, support of the ongoing investigation, and a general assembly in the near future.

The post Greek sports minister to meet with Greek federation board and new president Aggelos Papanikolaou appeared first on Eurohoops.

item.title: Virtus erases a 19-point deficit and wins a thriller against Milano in the Italian derby
item.dc:creator: Stefan Acevski

item.content:encoded:
By Stefan Acevski / info@eurohoops.net

Virtus Bologna achieved a victory in the fifth round of Legabasket as they defeated Olimpia Milano 98-94 in an away game after overtime.

Wendell Moore scored 27 points for the visitors, Trent Frazier added 17, Marcus Carr had 13 points and nine assists, while Mouhamet Diouf recorded a double-double with ten points and ten rebounds.

For the hosts, RJ Cole scored 19 points with seven assists, Jason Burnell had 16, Moses Wright 15, and Leandro Bolmaro 13.

It seemed that Olimpia would finally secure an important win, as they were up by 19 points (61-42) in the middle of the third quarter. However, with a 9-0 run at the end of the fourth quarter, Virtus got back into the game, took it to a dramatic finish, and eventually forced overtime.

There, Alex Mumbru’s team showed more concentration and took the victory from Milan, maintaining their perfect record in the league.

item.title: Parker on Partizan and Obradovic: “He took a risk with me, and I took a risk with him”
item.dc:creator: Stefan Acevski
item.description:
A former Partizan basketball player opened up about his time at the club, where he spoke about his relationship with Zeljko Obradovic, the chaos with the fans, and being kicked off the team

The post Parker on Partizan and Obradovic: “He took a risk with me, and I took a risk with him” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Stefan Acevski / info@eurohoops.net

The saga of Jabari Parker at Partizan has finally ended, as the two parties parted ways on Friday evening, following a not-so-great stint for Parker with the Serbian team.

Jabari came as a big signing, but his first season was very turbulent, and midway through it, he went on loan to Joventut. After that, he never wore the Partizan jersey again.

Now, the former second pick of the NBA draft shared his version of the story with “Sport Klub”, where he emphasized that Zeljko Obradovic was one of the main reasons for his arrival, and he was surprised that Obradovic left Partizan without a word.

“It was a specific experience. I wouldn’t say anyone is to blame. After all, we’re talking about a team. There are things I could have done better, just as there are things everyone could have done better. When you take on a commitment and commit to something, you need to persevere. I knew that when things weren’t going well, there was a temptation to give up. Everyone wanted to give up, to throw in the towel.

But then some things happened with the coach. He is the man who decided to resign. Why he did it, it’s up to him to explain. Maybe it’s important to make that clear. He never explained his decision to me. But I had a personal conversation with him, and he is a man who commands respect. He was one of the reasons I wanted to be part of Partizan. I wanted to take on that challenge, just as he took on the challenge with me. He took a risk with me, and I took a risk with him. That mutual commitment was important to me. When I saw he left, it surprised me. And then everything else started to fall apart.”

Parker noted that everything starts to collapse when the leader leaves the club.

“Everything always starts with the leader. My job as a player is to come to practice and, as best as I can, follow the instructions. When you remove the leader, the person everyone relies on, things become difficult.”

“Fans had bricks, stormed in, and broke into the facility”

One of the most stressful experiences Jabari had was after Zeljko Obradovic’s departure, when a large number of fans came in front of the arena with bricks, and Parker still wonders how the fans knew the training would take place, as it was at a different time than usual.

“What surprised me the most was seeing about 2,000 fans outside our training gym. They had bricks, stormed in, and broke into the facility, and they were threatening us. It almost seemed to me like it was all set up. Because who could have given them such information? Who could have told them when we would be there? It was very strange and suspicious to me that people who are not part of the team knew when we were coming to the gym, especially since we usually train in the morning. I don’t know, what would you think if you found yourself in a situation where your safety was threatened? Someone who knew about the training obviously passed that information to others…”

The American added that he doesn’t know why the fans did that, as the players were not to blame for Zeljko Obradovic’s departure.

“I don’t know why the fans did that. I don’t know why they were angry with us. We weren’t to blame for the coach’s departure. He knows he did what he thought was best for himself. He’s a grown man. He has the right to make his own decisions. He doesn’t owe anyone an explanation. And then we started losing games under the pressure of all that madness. Okay, fans can continue to support us in a positive way, but why would someone come to a game just to throw things at the players? Do you want us to win, or do you come already expecting the worst, with a preconceived decision to throw batteries, lighters, or beer at someone? That really hurt me.”

“I don’t know why I was separated from the team”

Jabari explained what happened since Joan Penarroya came to Partizan, revealing that he was told in just one training session that he would be practicing on the side, after which he was left out of the team the next day.

“Here’s how it happened. I had a heel injury. I think we were playing an ABA League game when I hurt my heel. Because of that, I was sidelined for a week. After that, I did a few training sessions during which I was gradually coming back to the team. And then, during one training session, the coach simply decided that I wouldn’t participate in the rest of the practice. He told me to go to the bike. I was making some mistakes because I hadn’t been with the team for a while, and in the meantime, new plays were introduced. He expected me to master them immediately. That’s why he told me to go to the bike.”

“Instead of the coach talking to me, he just informed me that I would be staying in Belgrade. Because of that, I didn’t travel to Munich, where the team played a game. That’s when I found out that I was out of the rotation. I was separated from the team. I don’t know why.”

The post Parker on Partizan and Obradovic: “He took a risk with me, and I took a risk with him” appeared first on Eurohoops.

item.title: Giannakopoulos on Olympiacos: “How can they abstain from the chance to clean up basketball?”
item.dc:creator: Aris Barkas
item.description:
The owner of Panathinaikos with new posts on his social media asks from Olympiacos to take action and presents his personal view on the future of the sport

The post Giannakopoulos on Olympiacos: “How can they abstain from the chance to clean up basketball?” appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Aris Barkas/ barkas@eurohoops.net

After official press releases on the Greek basketball scandal by Panathinaikos, Olympiacos, and AEK, and several public statements on the case, Dimitris Giannakopoulos made two social media posts about the case.

In the first, the owner of Panathinaikos asks the “eternal rival” Olympiacos to take more action on the case.

In the first post he writes the following:

“Fact 1: The owners of Olympiacos recently reminded us that it is the biggest team in Europe…”

“Fact 2: Jerseys and money were found in the possession of referees who are currently in prison for match-fixing.”

“Fact 3: In recent years, Olympiacos has intervened in support of these imprisoned referees, arguing that it was wrong for another team to raise concerns—concerns that have since been vindicated—regarding the unsuitability of these officials…”

“Fact 4: All of Greece watched the finals and either felt revulsion or expressed dismay—regardless of whether their own team won or lost—at the high-handed, arbitrary manner in which the matches were officiated by these imprisoned referees, whom Olympiacos had previously defended.”

“Fact 5: Olympiacos—arbitrarily, and without any prior incident or trouble in the basketball sphere—decides, in the name of a ‘legendary’ ‘cleansing’ of basketball, to humiliate itself. In doing so, it takes an extreme step—a move that the government of the time unfortunately had to contend with, forced to intervene so as not to be left exposed to the high-handed, bullying tactics of a club whose own owners—for reasons of their own—had relegated it to the A2 division.”

“Fact 6: I must acknowledge that the amount of money they have spent on complaints and legal proceedings—ostensibly in favor of ‘cleansing’ basketball—exceeds the total spent by all the rest of us combined.”

“Fact 7: Regarding all the titles won in recent years, one of these specific referees has officiated the overwhelming majority of the matches.”

“Fact 8: To this day—aside from making references to me and any statements I may have made—‘the biggest club in Europe’ has offered no response regarding all the aforementioned facts concerning basketball.” “THEY HAVE NO OPINION???”

“HOW CAN THEY ABSTAIN DURING THE GREATEST OPPORTUNITY TO DATE TO CLEAN UP BASKETBALL—ESPECIALLY NOW THAT THERE IS ACTUAL EVIDENCE, RATHER THAN JUST THE OPINIONS OF ZEALOUS OFFICIALS?”

“These questions are directed at you, and they will keep coming back—no matter how often you shift your agenda.”

“‘Legendary tough guys’ and ‘good boys’ shouldn’t be giving you any trouble.”

In his second post, Giannakopoulos talks about the future of the sport in Europe.

“A personal view—not focusing on legal compliance, but rather on what is best for basketball.”

“Liolios out: Liolios must go, as his judgment is clouded by arrogance and ego. It’s not about the money… He should be barred from any further involvement. He must fully disclose everything he knows (as the man at the top, he knows it all). This buys time for a new era in basketball… If that fails, then step in and seize everything.”

“Referees: A short prison sentence, provided they give a full account of the source of the bribes… otherwise, life imprisonment. Exemplary criminal penalties for those who paid the bribes—both legally and at the club level (including amateur clubs). A mandatory life ban for any referee who fails to report a colleague or a club official who attempts to offer a bribe.”

“Teams should be empowered to report—with evidence—any attempted match-fixing, and be rewarded in some way for doing so.”

“That would put an immediate, definitive end to it all.”

“And finally, the State should provide significant funding to the new Hellenic Basketball Federation and the Central Referees’ Committee to immediately develop a capable group of new referees.”

 

The post Giannakopoulos on Olympiacos: “How can they abstain from the chance to clean up basketball?” appeared first on Eurohoops.

item.title: Former Greek federation president Vaggelis Liolios remanded in custody
item.dc:creator: Aris Barkas
item.description:
The road for a new federation president has officially opened, after a written statement by Liolios to Greek authorities which was presented during his hearing

The post Former Greek federation president Vaggelis Liolios remanded in custody appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Aris Barkas/ barkas@eurohoops.net

Former Greek basketball federation president Vaggelis Liolios and former player turned businessman Giorgos Mavraganis arrived at 10.00 local time at the Evelpidon courthouse in Athens to be examined by the prosecutor, and more than 12 hours later, the authorities decided to remand them to custody until trial.

Upon his arrival, Liolios, with a written statement, informed the authorities that he ceased his involvement with basketball, at least during the legal proceedings.

Both are accused of bribery and match-fixing in a case that shocked the sport all over Europe, and after this move by Liolios, a new basketball federation president must be elected or appointed.

The consensus is that a personality with an impeccable record and worldwide prestige must be the new president, sending a message of change everywhere, and Panagiotis Giannakis is widely considered the best option.

Giannakis is expected to testify in the case on Monday.

His attorney, Andreas Mitsainas, revealed on Friday that the 67-year-old former player and national team coach intends to clear the air regarding recent reports in Greece about officiating calls directed against him.

“You know that Mr. Giannakis is a legend of Greek basketball. This whole situation is a dark cloud over Greek basketball. And he will personally contribute to exposing what took place, including what was done against him,” he mentioned.

The broader judicial probe spans a ten-year window from 2016 to 2026. It involves six suspects who face charges of bribery and unfair interference across roughly 50 suspicious games.

The post Former Greek federation president Vaggelis Liolios remanded in custody appeared first on Eurohoops.

item.title: Barcelona and Bayern not expected to attend meeting for NBA Europe, Madrid in contact
item.dc:creator: Aris Barkas
item.description:
Two EuroLeague clubs are keeping their distance from the NBA, while Real Madrid is more willing to listen

The post Barcelona and Bayern not expected to attend meeting for NBA Europe, Madrid in contact appeared first on Eurohoops.
item.content:encoded:
By Aris Barkas/ barkas@eurohoops.net

A crucial week is ahead for the NBA Europe project, according to reports from across Europe and information from Eurohoops sources.

As Sky Sports reported, a meeting is expected in London, where the Ballon d’Or ceremony will be held on Monday.

According to the British report, PSG, Bayern Munich, AC Milan, Barcelona and Real Madrid are expected to be attend, but Catalan newspaper “Sport” reveals that Barcelona and Bayern will not be part of the meeting.

Various sources have confirmed to EuroLeague that Barcelona and Bayern are keeping a firm stance, aligned with the decision taken in Como by the EuroLeague owners; on the other hand, Real Madrid seems to be the EuroLeague club more inclined to continue a dialogue with the NBA.

The numbers of the offer

The negative stance of the EuroLeague clubs can be explained by the numbers presented by “Sport”.

According to the report, the total offer to the EuroLeague shareholders was 520M euros to abolish the league and join the new project; This makes it 40M per club, and they would also lose ownership of the league.

On top of that, they also had to pay 400M euros each as a participation fee. Essentially, the EuroLeague clubs got only a discount on the minimum half-million bid that the NBA has set for participation in the new league, which means that, in theory, they need 40 M in revenue annually per club for the next decade, just to recover the participation fee.

 

The post Barcelona and Bayern not expected to attend meeting for NBA Europe, Madrid in contact appeared first on Eurohoops.
